Earnings snapshot and what changed for DLocal stock

DLocal (NasdaqGS:DLO) just posted its third quarter 2026 report, with higher sales, net income and earnings per share than a year earlier, alongside fresh commentary on volumes, regulation and foreign exchange pressure.

The firm reported third quarter sales of US$398.05 million compared with US$282.48 million a year earlier. Net income for the period was US$67.83 million versus US$51.83 million, with basic earnings per share from continuing operations at US$0.24 compared with US$0.18.

Diluted earnings per share from continuing operations came in at US$0.23 compared with US$0.17. For the first nine months of 2026, DLocal reported sales of US$1.13b compared with US$755.7 million a year earlier and net income of US$164.44 million versus US$141.27 million.

Across those nine months, basic earnings per share from continuing operations were US$0.57 compared with US$0.49, while diluted earnings per share were US$0.56 versus US$0.47. Management commentary pointed to strong total payment volume, deeper merchant relationships and improved operating leverage backing these headline figures.

Alongside the income statement, DLocal highlighted an expanded regulatory footprint with 42 licenses and registrations in 26 markets. That wider authorization base supports its cross border payment offering to global merchants across sectors such as commerce, streaming, ride hailing, financial services and gaming.

Guidance for total payment volume and gross profit was maintained, but management expects foreign exchange headwinds and softer conditions in some smaller markets to moderate operating profit growth for the full year. Currency effects in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina were singled out as key pressure points.

Market reaction around the announcement was mixed. The business beat one widely watched earnings per share estimate but posted revenue slightly below some analyst expectations, and the stock fell 2.9% in after hours trading on November 12, 2026 according to the provided data.

Beyond the income statement, DLocal also used its balance sheet more actively. The company repurchased about US$34.04 million of shares in the quarter and completed a wider buyback program, while also signing a US$150 million credit facility to fund general corporate uses, including further repurchases.

DLocal’s latest figures land against a share price that has eased in recent weeks, with a 30 day share price return of down 6.81% and a 90 day move of down 3.39%. Over a 1 year period the total shareholder return is up 1.78%, while the 5 year total shareholder return is down 60.66%. This points to fading short term momentum but a still mixed long term record as investors weigh strong payment volume growth against foreign exchange risks and the impact of buybacks at a US$13.69 share price.
